cards.q: Drug-drug interaction: description
cards.a: Modification of one drug's response by another given together or in quick succession

cards.q: Usual nature of a drug interaction's change in response
cards.a: Quantitative: intensity increased or decreased (sometimes qualitative, an abnormal response)

cards.q: Main factor raising the chance of drug interactions
cards.a: Number of drugs taken concurrently (polypharmacy)

cards.q: Regular medication classes most likely in interactions: list all
cards.a: Antidiabetics, antihypertensives, antianginals, antiarthritics, antiepileptics, antiparkinsonians, oral contraceptives, anticoagulants, antiasthmatics, psychopharmacological agents, antipeptic ulcer/reflux drugs, corticosteroids, antitubercular drugs, anti-HIV drugs

cards.q: Interaction-prone drugs with a narrow safety margin
cards.a: Aminoglycoside antibiotics, digoxin, lithium

cards.q: Interaction-prone drugs affecting closely regulated functions
cards.a: Antihypertensives, antidiabetics, anticoagulants

cards.q: Interaction-prone highly plasma protein-bound drugs
cards.a: NSAIDs, oral anticoagulants, sulfonylureas

cards.q: Interaction-prone drugs metabolised by saturation kinetics
cards.a: Phenytoin, theophylline

cards.q: Two broad mechanism categories of drug interaction
cards.a: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic

cards.q: Pharmacokinetic interaction: what it alters
cards.a: Concentration of the object drug at its site of action (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion), hence response intensity

cards.q: Pharmacokinetic interaction sites: list all
cards.a: Absorption or first-pass metabolism; plasma protein displacement; tissue binding (volume of distribution, clearance); inhibition or induction of metabolism; excretion

cards.q: Pharmacodynamic interaction: what it alters
cards.a: Action at the target site with no change in concentration: synergism, antagonism or an abnormal response

cards.q: Pharmaceutical (in-vitro) interaction: where it occurs
cards.a: Injectables mixed in one syringe or infusion bottle before administration

cards.q: Penicillin G or ampicillin mixed with an aminoglycoside: result
cards.a: Inactivation (do not mix parenteral drugs)

cards.q: Thiopentone mixed in one bottle with
cards.a: Succinylcholine or morphine

cards.q: Heparin mixed in one bottle with
cards.a: Penicillin, gentamicin or hydrocortisone

cards.q: Noradrenaline added to
cards.a: Sodium bicarbonate solution (inactivated)

cards.q: Advice on mixing parenteral drugs
cards.a: Avoid mixing two or more parenteral drugs before injecting

cards.q: Does a possible interaction contraindicate concurrent use?
cards.a: Not necessarily: knowing the mechanism may allow use with dose adjustment or other corrective measures

cards.q: Polypharmacy: definition
cards.a: Regular use of five or more medicines

cards.q: Polypharmacy: why it is common in
cards.a: Elderly patients with multiple chronic diseases (diabetes, hypertension)

cards.q: Polypharmacy control: prescribing measures
cards.a: Detailed drug history, rational prescribing, restrict polypharmacy, simplify regimen

cards.q: Usual mechanism of interaction affecting oral absorption
cards.a: Insoluble, poorly absorbed complexes form in the gut lumen

cards.q: Antibiotic class whose absorption falls with calcium, iron, antacids or sucralfate
cards.a: Tetracyclines

cards.q: Gap between tetracycline and calcium, iron or antacid doses
cards.a: 2 to 3 hours

cards.q: Phenytoin absorption reduced by
cards.a: Sucralfate (binds in the gut lumen)

cards.q: Ketoconazole absorption reduced by
cards.a: H2 blockers and proton pump inhibitors (less gastric acid for dissolution)

cards.q: Antibiotics that reduce gut flora and so steroid contraceptive recycling: list all
cards.a: Ampicillin, tetracyclines, cotrimoxazole

cards.q: Mechanism of contraceptive failure with broad-spectrum antibiotics
cards.a: Gut flora no longer deconjugates steroid glucuronides, so enterohepatic recycling falls

cards.q: Drugs that alter gut motility and so absorption: list all
cards.a: Atropinic drugs, tricyclic antidepressants, opioids, prokinetics (metoclopramide)

cards.q: Property making a drug prone to protein-binding displacement
cards.a: High plasma protein binding with a small volume of distribution

cards.q: Drugs particularly liable to displacement interactions
cards.a: Coumarin anticoagulants, sulfonylureas, certain NSAIDs, antiepileptics

cards.q: Requirement on the displacing drug
cards.a: Binds the same plasma protein site with higher affinity

cards.q: Why displacement usually raises steady-state levels only marginally
cards.a: Free drug is quickly distributed, metabolised and excreted

cards.q: When displacement becomes clinically significant
cards.a: When tissue binding is also displaced, or metabolism or excretion is inhibited

cards.q: Quinidine and digoxin: effect on digoxin levels
cards.a: Nearly doubles blood levels (less tissue binding and renal/biliary clearance), causing toxicity

cards.q: Sulfonamides and cotrimoxazole raise toxicity of: list all
cards.a: Phenytoin, warfarin, sulfonylureas

cards.q: Antiepileptics and albumin: interaction
cards.a: Displace each other from albumin, raising free levels and toxicity

cards.q: Aspirin displaces which drug from albumin
cards.a: Tolbutamide

cards.q: Sulfonamides displace bilirubin from albumin in neonates: risk
cards.a: Kernicterus (bilirubin enters the immature brain)

cards.q: Antibiotic that displaces bilirubin when used under one month of age
cards.a: Ceftriaxone (kernicterus risk)

cards.q: Two drug parameters changed by metabolic interactions
cards.a: Bioavailability (first-pass metabolism) and plasma half-life (if mainly metabolised)

cards.q: Mechanism of metabolic inhibition by a second drug
cards.a: Competition for the same CYP450 isoenzyme or cofactor

cards.q: Metabolic inhibition matters most for drugs cleared by
cards.a: Saturation kinetics

cards.q: Important inhibitors of drug metabolism: list all
cards.a: Macrolide antibiotics, azole antifungals, chloramphenicol, omeprazole, SSRIs, HIV protease inhibitors, cimetidine, ciprofloxacin, metronidazole

cards.q: Statin myopathy risk is increased by: list all
cards.a: Fibrates, niacin, erythromycin, azole antifungals, HIV protease inhibitors

cards.q: Why propranolol prolongs lidocaine's half-life
cards.a: Reduces hepatic blood flow, and lidocaine metabolism depends on that flow

cards.q: Speed of enzyme inhibition
cards.a: Quick (develops soon after the inhibitor is given)

cards.q: Time for enzyme induction to reach maximal effect
cards.a: 1 to 2 weeks of the inducer

cards.q: Time for induction to regress after the inducer is stopped
cards.a: Gradually over 1 to 3 weeks

cards.q: Microsomal enzyme inducers: list all
cards.a: Barbiturates, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampin, cigarette smoking, chronic alcoholism, certain pollutants

cards.q: Enzyme inducers, review-book list: list all
cards.a: Nevirapine, St John's wort, carbamazepine, charcoal-broiled meat, rifampicin, chronic alcohol, phenytoin, griseofulvin, phenobarbitone, smoking

cards.q: Clinical consequence of enzyme induction (two examples)
cards.a: Contraceptive failure and loss of effect of other drugs

cards.q: Why paracetamol is more toxic in chronic alcoholics and in those on enzyme inducers
cards.a: Toxic dose is lower because a metabolite causes the overdose hepatotoxicity

cards.q: Paracetamol daily dose considered safe in chronic alcoholics
cards.a: Less than 3 g/day

cards.q: Probenecid effect on penicillins and cephalosporins
cards.a: Blocks tubular secretion, prolonging their half-life

cards.q: Clinical use of the probenecid-penicillin interaction
cards.a: Single-dose treatment of gonorrhoea

cards.q: Aspirin effect on probenecid's uricosuric action
cards.a: Blocks it

cards.q: Aspirin effect on methotrexate excretion
cards.a: Reduces tubular secretion of methotrexate

cards.q: Clinical use of urine pH change for weak acids and bases
cards.a: Hastens excretion in poisoning

cards.q: Drugs that raise lithium levels: list all
cards.a: Diuretics (main), tetracyclines, ACE inhibitors, certain NSAIDs

cards.q: Antimicrobials that decrease lithium excretion
cards.a: Metronidazole and tinidazole

cards.q: P-glycoprotein inhibitors (review mnemonic QVACKER): list all
cards.a: Quinidine, verapamil, amiodarone, cyclosporin, ketoconazole, erythromycin or clarithromycin, ritonavir

cards.q: P-glycoprotein inducer
cards.a: Rifampicin

cards.q: Effect of a P-glycoprotein inhibitor on digoxin
cards.a: Raised digoxin levels, toxicity and arrhythmias

cards.q: Effect of rifampicin (P-gp inducer) on digoxin
cards.a: Increased urinary excretion of digoxin, reducing its effect

cards.q: Drugs whose levels rise with CYP3A4 inhibitors (erythromycin, clarithromycin, azoles): list all
cards.a: Phenytoin, carbamazepine, warfarin, sulfonylureas, diazepam, theophylline, cyclosporine, HIV protease inhibitors

cards.q: Drugs whose efficacy falls with enzyme inducers (phenobarbitone, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampin): list all
cards.a: Warfarin, corticosteroids, oral contraceptives, sulfonylureas, antidepressants, metronidazole, doxycycline, chloramphenicol, protease inhibitors

cards.q: CYP enzyme inhibited by isoniazid (all except one)
cards.a: All CYP enzymes except CYP2E1

cards.q: CYP enzyme that converts paracetamol to its hepatotoxic metabolite
cards.a: CYP2E1 (forms NAPQI)

cards.q: Rifampicin effect on oral contraceptives and management
cards.a: Estrogen degraded, contraceptive failure: increase estrogen dose or use a barrier method

cards.q: Rifampicin effect on warfarin and the alternative
cards.a: Reduced warfarin effect; replace with heparin

cards.q: Strongest CYP3A4 inhibitor among protease inhibitors
cards.a: Ritonavir (irreversible inhibitor)

cards.q: Rifampicin effect on sofosbuvir
cards.a: Reduces its effect (P-gp induction)

cards.q: Antiepileptic that inhibits CYP (exception to the enzyme-inducer class)
cards.a: Valproate

cards.q: Antiepileptics that are CYP enzyme inducers: list all
cards.a: Carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbitone

cards.q: Combinations causing additive CNS depression with alcohol: list all partners
cards.a: Benzodiazepine, sedating antihistamine, neuroleptic, opioid

cards.q: Result of additive CNS depressant combinations
cards.a: Excessive sedation, respiratory depression, motor incoordination

cards.q: Drugs with alpha-blockers that cause excessive BP fall and fainting: list all
cards.a: Vasodilators, ACE inhibitors, high-ceiling diuretics, cardiac depressants

cards.q: Propranolol with insulin or sulfonylureas: hazard
cards.a: Pronounced, often silent hypoglycaemia (blocks recovery and warning symptoms)

cards.q: Ceftriaxone or cefoperazone with warfarin
cards.a: Additive prolongation of prothrombin time and bleeding

cards.q: Carbenicillin or ticarcillin with aspirin or clopidogrel
cards.a: Excessive platelet inhibition and bleeding

cards.q: Propranolol with digoxin in a digitalised patient
cards.a: Marked bradycardia

cards.q: Mechanism of the sildenafil-nitrate interaction
cards.a: Nitrates raise cGMP; sildenafil (PDE5 inhibitor) blocks its breakdown

cards.q: Sildenafil or tadalafil with organic nitrates: result and status
cards.a: Precipitous BP fall and myocardial ischaemia; concurrent use contraindicated

cards.q: ACE inhibitor with potassium-sparing diuretic: risk
cards.a: Severe hyperkalaemia

cards.q: Bactericidal beta-lactam combined with bacteriostatic tetracycline: result
cards.a: Antagonism of the bactericidal action

cards.q: Mutual antagonists at the bacterial 50S ribosome: list all
cards.a: Macrolides, clindamycin, chloramphenicol

cards.q: NSAIDs blunting ACE inhibitor, ARB or diuretic effect: mechanism
cards.a: Inhibition of renal prostaglandin synthesis

cards.q: Aspirin blunting spironolactone: mechanism
cards.a: Reduces tubular secretion of canrenone, its active metabolite

cards.q: Dopamine blockers that antagonise levodopa: list all
cards.a: Neuroleptics (e.g. chlorpromazine, haloperidol) and metoclopramide

cards.q: Alcohol with metronidazole or cefoperazone
cards.a: Disulfiram-like reaction (bizarre, distressing symptoms)

cards.q: Ampicillin with allopurinol
cards.a: High incidence of skin rashes; avoid concurrent use

cards.q: Tricyclic antidepressants with adrenaline in local anaesthetic
cards.a: Potentiated BP rise (neuronal uptake inhibition); use plain local anaesthetic

cards.q: Chlorpromazine or TCAs with morphine, pethidine or codeine
cards.a: Enhanced CNS and respiratory depression; avoid concurrent use

cards.q: Levodopa-carbidopa with ACE inhibitors, vasodilators or prazosin
cards.a: Excessive postural hypotension; reduce antihypertensive dose

cards.q: Cimetidine or isoniazid with diazepam
cards.a: Inhibited benzodiazepine metabolism: exaggerated CNS depression; avoid or reduce dose

cards.q: Lidocaine with beta-blockers: effect
cards.a: Enhanced bradycardia and hypotension; avoid concurrent use

cards.q: Lidocaine with quinidine or other antiarrhythmics: effect
cards.a: Exaggerated cardiac depression and arrhythmias; avoid concurrent use

cards.q: Ciprofloxacin with theophylline
cards.a: Inhibited metabolism: theophylline toxicity; monitor and reduce dose

cards.q: Warfarin: drugs that inhibit its metabolism (bleeding risk): list all
cards.a: Metronidazole, tinidazole, ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin, pefloxacin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, ketoconazole, itraconazole, fluconazole, chloramphenicol, allopurinol

cards.q: Ampicillin or amoxicillin raising warfarin bleeding risk: mechanism
cards.a: Reduced gut flora lowers vitamin K production in the gut

cards.q: Sulfonamides or cotrimoxazole with warfarin: three mechanisms
cards.a: Displacement, inhibited metabolism, and reduced gut vitamin K production

cards.q: Aspirin or clopidogrel with warfarin or heparin: result
cards.a: Increased bleeding risk

cards.q: Enzyme inducers with warfarin: effect
cards.a: Loss of anticoagulant efficacy (rifampin, barbiturates, phenytoin, carbamazepine)

cards.q: Allopurinol with azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine: action
cards.a: Inhibits their metabolism: reduce the dose to one-third

cards.q: Allopurinol with ampicillin or amoxicillin
cards.a: Increased incidence of rashes; avoid concurrent use

cards.q: Tetracyclines with oral contraceptives: result and advice
cards.a: Enterohepatic circulation interrupted; contraceptive failure; advise alternative contraception

cards.q: Furosemide with aminoglycosides: result
cards.a: Additive ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity; avoid concurrent use

cards.q: Diuretic-induced hypokalaemia with digoxin: prevention
cards.a: Give a potassium-sparing diuretic or potassium supplement

cards.q: Ciprofloxacin with an NSAID: serious risk
cards.a: Enhanced CNS toxicity and seizures

cards.q: NSAIDs with sulfonylureas, phenytoin, valproate or methotrexate
cards.a: Displacement and reduced elimination: toxicity; substitute paracetamol

cards.q: NSAIDs with alcohol or corticosteroids
cards.a: Gastric mucosal damage and bleeding; concurrent use contraindicated

cards.q: Triptans with SSRIs, TCAs or other serotonergic drugs: risk
cards.a: Serotonin syndrome

cards.q: Tyramine-rich food with a non-selective MAO inhibitor: reaction
cards.a: Cheese reaction: hypertensive crisis (tyramine releases noradrenaline)

cards.q: Ephedrine (cough and cold remedies) with a non-selective MAO inhibitor
cards.a: Hypertensive crisis

cards.q: Tramadol or linezolid with a MAO inhibitor
cards.a: Serotonin syndrome

cards.q: MAO inhibitor with SSRI or SNRI: rule
cards.a: Never combine (serotonin syndrome)

cards.q: Washout before an SSRI after stopping an MAO inhibitor
cards.a: 2 weeks (fluoxetine: 5 weeks; SNRI: 1 week)

cards.q: Reversible MAO-A inhibitor with little tyramine risk
cards.a: Moclobemide (no dietary restriction needed)

cards.q: Cisapride, astemizole or terfenadine with erythromycin or ketoconazole: result
cards.a: Raised levels, QT prolongation and torsades de pointes (these drugs are banned)

cards.q: Grapefruit juice constituents that inhibit CYP3A4
cards.a: Naringin and furanocoumarins

cards.q: Why terfenadine was withdrawn from the market
cards.a: CYP3A4 inhibition (e.g. erythromycin, grapefruit juice) raised parent drug levels, causing fatal arrhythmias

cards.q: Deliberate beneficial combinations: ACE inhibitor plus diuretic treats
cards.a: Hypertension (synergistic action)

cards.q: Deliberate synergistic antibacterial pair
cards.a: Sulfamethoxazole plus trimethoprim

cards.q: Furosemide plus amiloride: purpose
cards.a: Prevents hypokalaemia

cards.q: Adrenaline added to lidocaine: purpose
cards.a: Local anaesthesia

cards.q: Purpose of combining antitubercular drugs
cards.a: Prevents drug resistance

cards.q: Interaction-prevention step before prescribing
cards.a: Record all current medication of the patient, from a detailed drug history

cards.q: When to consider interactions
cards.a: Whenever a drug is added to what the patient already takes

cards.q: Corrective measures for a significant interaction: list all
cards.a: Dose adjustment, staggered administration (2-3 h gap), monitoring, substitution (e.g. paracetamol for an NSAID), avoid combination

cards.q: Laboratory monitoring for interactions: list all
cards.a: INR (warfarin), lithium level, digoxin and potassium levels

cards.q: Therapeutic drug monitoring: information it gives
cards.a: Efficacy, compliance, drug-drug interactions, avoidance of toxicity, therapy cessation
